about: What the founder wants the cloud transcript provider measured on (ADR-039). Entries point at files that already exist in the repository's generated or committed test sets where one exists; where none exists the entry says so. Nothing here is uploaded unless the founder runs the harness with --i-have-founder-approval and names the entries.
privateRule: Every file under web/tests/media/real/ is the founder's own video: private: true, refused without --allow-private (the harness also enforces this by path, whatever this file says).
measured: durationS is the length of the audio stream that ffprobe reports for the file on disk (the harness's own probeDurationS), measured on 2026-10-11 (approxDurationS repeats it: the harness uses it for the estimate when a file is not on the machine). expectedSpeakers is filled only where the dataset itself says how many people speak; expectedSpeakersNote says where the number comes from.

generated.web/tests/media/speech/manifest.json: node web/spike/asr/prepare-speech.mjs (FLEURS, CC BY 4.0: 12 Turkish and 6 English read sentences; fetches the leading 26 MB + 16 MB of two tarballs)
generated.web/tests/media/speech/manifest-real.jso: node web/spike/asr/prepare-english.mjs (LibriSpeech test-clean 347 MB + alignments 623 MB, CC BY 4.0), then node web/scripts/transcript/prepare-realistic.mjs --set=val (AMI CC BY 4.0, Earnings-22 CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons music and sounds; see web/tests/media/SPEECH_SOURCE.md). On Windows run both from PowerShell, not Git Bash: they call `tar`, which must be the Windows one.
generated.web/tests/media/speech/manifest-cloud.js: node cloud/harness/prepare-extra.mjs (FLEURS ja_jp CC BY 4.0: leading 16 MB; MediaSpeech Turkish, OpenSLR SLR108, CC BY 4.0: leading 80 MB; two LibriSpeech readers from the pool above)

entries.note: The nearest open, login-free stand-in for spontaneous Turkish — NOT one two-way conversation (see turkish-conversation). The reference is lower case, without punctuation, numbers written as words ("covid ondokuz"): a provider that writes "19" is counted wrong by the strict measure, so read this WER as an upper bound.

entries.title: Spontaneous two-way Turkish conversation, 10–20 minutes, with a reference transcript
entries.howToGet: no open, login-free source with a trustworthy reference chosen (11 Oct 2026). Considered from what is known of these corpora — only MediaSpeech was actually fetched and checked today: Common Voice (CC0, but read sentences and a login/terms click); VoxPopuli (no transcribed Turkish set); MediaSpeech (used as turkish-media-speech: unrelated ~15 s segments, not a conversation); YODAS (CC BY, YouTube with uploader subtitles — not a trustworthy reference); LDC/Babel/CALLHOME-style corpora (paid or licence-gated). What would work: a 10–20 minute recording the founder makes with a second person and transcribes (or corrects from the on-device transcript).

entries.title: 10 read Japanese sentences (FLEURS ja_jp), joined; scored by character error rate
entries.expectedSpeakersNote: not known exactly: FLEURS gives no speaker ids. 10 recordings (1 marked FEMALE, 9 MALE), so at least 2 and at most 10 voices
entries.note: CER after NFKC, punctuation and spaces removed on both sides. Kanji numerals against digits and kana/kanji spelling choices are counted as errors (no Japanese text normaliser): read the CER as an upper bound.

entries.title: Spontaneous Japanese conversation with a reference transcript
entries.howToGet: no open, login-free source with a trustworthy reference chosen (11 Oct 2026). Considered from what is known of these corpora — none was fetched today, so each should be re-checked before it is ruled out for good: CEJC and CSJ (paid / licence agreement); CALLHOME Japanese (TalkBank account or LDC); ReazonSpeech (TV recordings, access terms); TEDxJP-10K (CC BY-NC-ND, built from YouTube); YODAS (uploader subtitles — not a trustworthy reference); Common Voice (read, login). What would work: a recording the founder is allowed to use with a human-made transcript — or a listening check only, without an error rate.

entries.title: Exactly two people (a man and a woman) taking turns and talking over each other at every change, with word times and who-said-what
entries.note: Synthetic: two READ voices laid over each other, not a real conversation (meeting-overlap-4 is the real one). 95 of 264 reference words lie inside an overlap; there the reference order (by word start) is a convention, so a provider that writes the two voices one after the other is charged some word-order errors. The speaker count (2) is the clean check here.
